remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was provided after the initial report.
The known 1.1 percentage-point miss affects a named launch use case, which the policy text treats as potentially material.
Legal review on disclosure remains open.
The current record does not show completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support readiness but do not satisfy the separate materiality/disclosure predicate.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed its claim to a caveated reading of the same record. That clarification is analytically useful, but it does not resolve the core compliance predicate identified in the initial report. On the available evidence, aggregate readiness passed and rehearsal did not produce severity-one incidents, which supports operational readiness. But the same record still shows a miss in a named launch use case, open legal review, and no evidence of completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance. Under the provided policy text, product framing such as non-core or low-volume does not resolve materiality in that circumstance. That means the record can support a weak, caveated readiness narrative, but not a compliant or compliant_with_caveats verdict on policy satisfaction, because the caveat here is not merely descriptive; it is an unresolved policy condition.
